findings.current: I had only ever dealt with D-rank Gates myself, so this was my first time seeing anything higher.
findings.defect: The draft says Taekyung has dealt only with D-rank Gates, while the source says D-rank is the highest Grade he has experienced.
findings.rationale: 고작 marks D-rank as the upper limit of his prior Gate experience, not the only Grade he has encountered.
findings.replacement: D-rank was as high as I’d ever gone myself, so this was my first time seeing anything higher.
findings.source: 물론 나야 D급 게이트가 고작이라 더 높은 등급은 처음이지만 사람들이 그렇다더라.

findings.current: Whether I offended you or not, it’s a fact. What’s there to be offended about?
findings.defect: The draft reverses who might have been offended. Team Leader Choi apologized for potentially offending Im Changsoo, and Changsoo replies that he himself has no reason to be offended.
findings.rationale: The omitted subject of 상하고 is Im Changsoo, the recipient of Choi’s preceding apology; it does not mean that Changsoo may have offended Choi.
findings.replacement: Why would I be offended? It’s the truth.
findings.source: “상하고 말고 할 게 있나 사실인데, 뭘.

findings.current: For a martial artist, that would be close to First Rate. But if I fought them, I would have to account for all sorts of variables.
findings.defect: The draft lowers the Minotaurs’ equivalent martial-arts classification from near 초일류 to near First Rate, despite rendering 초일류 as Top-tier earlier in the same chapter.
findings.rationale: The source distinguishes 초일류 from 일류, so collapsing both into First Rate changes the stated power hierarchy.
findings.replacement: For a martial artist, that would be close to Top-tier. But if I fought them, I would have to account for all sorts of variables.
findings.source: 무인이라면 초일류에 가까운 레벨이지만 놈들과 싸운다면 여러 가지 변수를 고려해야 한다.

findings.current: “For a C-rank with fuck-all to his name, you sure were going on about what you could do with a Minotaur and whatnot. You were practically writing a novel.”
findings.defect: The draft makes Im Changsoo explicitly accuse Taekyung of claiming what he could do against a Minotaur. The source derisively leaves the subject vague, saying only that he was going on about Minotaurs.
findings.rationale: 미노타우로스를 어쩌고저쩌고 deliberately summarizes the conversation without specifying a boast or claim of capability.
findings.replacement: “For a C-rank with fuck-all to his name, you sure had a lot to say about Minotaurs and whatnot. You were practically writing a novel.”
findings.source: “쥐뿔도 없는 C급 주제에 미노타우로스를 어쩌고저쩌고. 아주 소설을 쓰시던데.”

findings.current: Martial artists learned cultivation techniques that allowed them to use the energy inside their bodies efficiently, then maximized it through martial arts.
findings.defect: The generic word “energy” fails to preserve the chapter’s distinction between a martial artist’s qi and a Hunter’s mana.
findings.rationale: Here 기운 is explicitly the internal power used by martial artists through cultivation techniques and martial arts, so the required term is “qi.”
findings.replacement: Martial artists learned cultivation techniques that allowed them to use the qi inside their bodies efficiently, then maximized it through martial arts.
findings.source: 무인들은 신체 내부의 기운을 효율적으로 사용할 수 있는 내공심법을 익혔고 그걸 무공을 통해 극대화시켰다.

findings.current: Of course, it was on a completely different scale from an F-rank Gate.
findings.defect: The draft generalizes a specific comparison of ceiling height into an unspecified difference in scale.
findings.rationale: 높이 specifically describes the cavern ceiling’s height, continuing the immediately preceding observation about looking upward.
findings.replacement: Of course, the ceiling was incomparably higher than in an F-rank Gate.
findings.source: 물론 F급 게이트와는 차원이 다른 높이였다.

findings.defect: “Illusion” suggests a visual or supernatural phenomenon, whereas 착각 here means that Taekyung wonders whether he imagined or misperceived the vibration.
findings.rationale: The uncertainty concerns whether the faint physical sensation was real, not whether he saw an illusion.

findings.defect: “Ugh” expresses disgust or discomfort, while 에게 is a dismissive reaction to how underwhelmingly little appeared.
findings.rationale: The reaction sets up the observation that only one Minotaur emerged and conveys disappointment rather than revulsion.

findings.defect: The fourth Minotaur’s bellow is omitted between its footsteps and the Hunters’ reaction.
findings.rationale: The repeated bellow confirms another Minotaur emerging from the fourth hole and maintains the escalating entrance pattern.
findings.source:
쿵. 쿵.

- 음모오.

“아니, 시바. 뭐야, 이거.”

findings.current: “No way. It’s not like this is an Olympic athlete roll call.”
findings.defect: “Roll call” does not naturally evoke athletes being introduced by numbered lanes, weakening the setup for the following “lane five” joke.
findings.rationale: 선수 소개 means an athlete introduction, which directly motivates Taekyung’s subsequent reference to lane five.
findings.replacement: “No way. It’s not like they’re introducing Olympic athletes.”

findings.current: Something pricked at the corner of my chest.
findings.defect: The draft is an unnatural anatomical calque and obscures Taekyung’s sudden unease at having his concealed ability noticed.
findings.rationale: 가슴 한구석이 뜨끔했다 idiomatically describes an inward pang from feeling exposed or called out, not a literal prick in one corner of the chest.
findings.replacement: I felt a sudden twinge of unease.
findings.source: 나도 모르게 가슴 한구석이 뜨끔 했다.

summary: The draft contains two scene-fact or subject errors, one altered power classification, one over-explicit accusation, and several localized omissions or wording problems.
